session_tail:
erdict_from` checked a finding's quoted evidence with an exact substring match (`ev not in text`). When the model quoted a line from the skill file that was broken across two lines, it rejoined it into one. That one-character difference made a quote that really was in the file fail.

**The fix:** before comparing, both the evidence and the skill text now have every run of spaces, tabs and newlines turned into a single space (`" ".join(s.split())`). The 12-character minimum is checked after that, so padding a short quote with spaces doesn't get it through. Word order still has to match, so the tests for reordered words and made-up quotes still fail as they should. `scripts/library.py` also reads the evidence, but only to print it, so it didn't need changing.

**Tests:** after the fix, `python3 tests/test_validate.py` prints 55 PASS lines and no FAIL lines. I also ran every other file in `tests/` and none of them failed. Nothing is committed.

**Distillation:** I followed the skill's steps and skipped only step 2 (novelty), as you asked. None of the other steps stopped me.
- **Duplicate check:** no existing skills in either location.
- **Scope:** `project`, because the check it uses, `python3 tests/test_validate.py`, only exists in this repo. Without the fix, the rewrapped-quote test fails; if matching gets too loose, the reordered-words and absent-evidence tests fail.
- **Where the bug came from:** I left out `introduced_by`. The exact match was already there in the `baseline` commit, so no later commit introduced it.
- **Secret scan:** clean.
- **Self-review:** it passed every criterion except novelty, so I saved it unedited with `--decision approved` and a reason saying it was self-reviewed.
- **Saved to:** `.claude/skillforge/skills/whitespace-insensitive-evidence-quotes/SKILL.md`. It's in the warm tier (not yet proven).

The Gamma and Google Calendar connectors need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they'll work; this task didn't need them.
